newsitem.title: USA: Hamilton County plans early fall stadium issuance.
newsitem.headline: Hamilton County plans early fall stadium issuance.

text.p: Hamilton County hopes to make at least a partial issuance of sales tax bonds for a new Cincinnati Bengals football stadium in late summer or early fall, county Administrator David Krings said Monday.

The projected $270 million stadium is to be financed by about $180 million of sales tax bonds from the county as well as contributions from Ohio and the National Football League franchise, Krings said.
Hamilton County recently received requests for proposal responses from underwriters for its issuance and hopes to announce the selection of a syndicate for the deal by the end of July, Krings said.
Krings said officials have not decided whether the likely negotiated deal will be completed in one or multiple issuances.

The bonds for the stadium are being backed by half-cent increase in the county sales tax approved by voters for partial financing of stadiums for the Bengals and the Cincinnati Reds baseball team and provide some property tax relief, Krings said.
Public Finance Management Inc of Philadelphiffer & Williams PLL of Cincinnati is serving as bond counsel.
Ohio is expected to contribute about $36 million and the Bengals from $50 million to $60 million toward the financing of the stadium, scheduled for completion in August 2000, Krings said.
No site has been selected for the new Reds stadium and financing terms have not been completed for the ballpark, Krings said.
